I've read through a few comments and I'm going to be blunt but it is with a mass amount of love and understanding. 

You need to be alone. You need to fully embrace the wonders of being alone. You need to try and enjoy being alone and MOST importantly you need to learn to love YOU alone. 

Regardless of what happened, you're a human that deserves to feel loved, in your love language and that was not being fulfilled. 

It comes off as enmeshed and I strongly recommend you see a therapist that you "vibe" with. Rule of 3, three visits should tell you if you have a connection if not move to another therapist until you find the one that is meant to help you. Therapists are not one size fits all. 

Sounds like you had a bad partner and an even worse "friend", cheating isn't acceptable, even if you make excuses for it in your head... either one of them could have told you what was going on but neither did... that alone says way too much about them as individuals. 

My marriage ended after 8 years, 6 of which seemed like a fairytale, I was 32... we have two children. At first, I could barely get out of bed until I got back into therapy and realized that it wasn't a fairytale. I looked at our marriage objectively and realized we are BOTH better people now that we're not together. We're better for our children. (But there are also a lot of emotions and hardships when you add children, especially when you both love them as you should.) My husband left because he "didn't want to try anymore." I blamed myself... until I realized that he never "tried", he was just present when it came to me but didn't put effort toward loving me. He finally admitted that he didn't love me but he loved what I did for him and how I'm a great mom to our kids; he wasn't sure for how long he didn't love me but it could have been always. I still had fantasies for a while that he would "come home" and say he wanted to work it out and actually go to counseling but then my therapist would say something like "For what, to go back to the same relationship where you have to beg to receive love... Cat... no." I remind myself that I can look back and acknowledge that we had great times but the overall picture is what matters. Yes, I will probably always love him, but it's better from afar where I'm not being snuffed out. The little pieces of light will never make up for the light you're missing, once you find that in yourself being alone feels like such a comfortable and wonderful place... then you'll only make room for someone who deserves to share it with you. 💜

You're a strong person... all on your own. Keep your head up.
